name: New Mexico
nameStory: Here is the fact that fixes it forever: New Mexico is older than Mexico. Spaniards named the region Nuevo Mexico in the 1560s, more than 250 years before the country of Mexico won independence and took that name. It is not named after the country next door.
capitalStory: Santa Fe means 'Holy Faith.' Founded in 1610, it is the oldest capital city in the United States - older than Plymouth Colony - and at 7,199 feet it is also the highest.

majorFeatures.name: Rio Grande
majorFeatures.note: Splits the state and becomes the border

majorFeatures.name: White Sands
majorFeatures.note: 275 square miles of white gypsum dunes

funFacts: Santa Fe has been a capital city under Spain, Mexico, and the United States without ever moving.
The first atomic bomb was detonated at the Trinity site in the New Mexico desert on July 16, 1945.
White Sands is made of gypsum, not quartz, which is why it stays cool enough to walk on barefoot.
New Mexico's constitution has specific protections for Spanish speakers, a condition of its 1912 statehood.
whyItMatters: The Rio Grande is not just a river - for about 1,250 miles it is the international boundary with Mexico. A river that shifts its channel makes a poor border, and disputes over where exactly it runs have required treaties to settle. It is the physical fact underneath most US immigration debate.
